question: Your coordinator agent's loop ends whenever a response from Claude contains any assistant text. In testing, the coordinator often stops after writing a short note such as "Next I'll ask the web search subagent for more sources," and the cited report is never produced. Which change to the loop's control flow fixes this most reliably?

options.text: End the loop when a response contains assistant text that is longer than 200 words, treating long text as the final answer.
options.reason: The guide names checking for assistant text content as a completion indicator as an anti-pattern; text length does not show that the task is finished.

options.text: Ignore assistant text and run the loop for a fixed cap of 15 iterations, which the team chooses as the main stopping rule.
options.reason: The guide names an arbitrary iteration cap as the primary stopping mechanism as an anti-pattern; it can stop work early or run needless iterations.

options.text: Continue the loop while stop_reason is "tool_use" and end the loop only when stop_reason is "end_turn".
options.reason: The guide says loop control should continue on "tool_use" and terminate on "end_turn", because stop_reason is the reliable completion signal.

options.text: End the loop only when the assistant text contains a completion phrase such as "final report ready," which the system prompt tells the coordinator to write.
options.reason: The guide names parsing natural language signals to decide loop termination as an anti-pattern, so this replaces one unreliable signal with another.
